item.text:
**3B.5 Research Note: Ali Khamenei (2024)**

**Bottom line:** The 2024 record is overwhelmingly negative on this lens. I found strong evidence of surveillance-heavy, punitive, and coercive administrative control, especially around compulsory veiling. The only clear positive items were discretionary prisoner pardons/commutations, which show occasional clemency but not a lawful, rights-protective emergency framework.

| Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| [Iran: Draconian campaign to enforce compulsory veiling laws through surveillance and mass car confiscations](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/iran-draconian-campaign-to-enforce-compulsory-veiling-laws-through-surveillance-and-mass-car-confiscations/) | Amnesty International | 2024-03-06 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/03/iran-draconian-campaign-to-enforce-compulsory-veiling-laws-through-surveillance-and-mass-car-confiscations/ | Iran’s authorities used widespread surveillance, mass police checks, car confiscations, prosecutions, flogging, and “morality” classes to enforce veiling rules. This is strong evidence of security-administrative control being used for intimidation and punishment, not narrowly lawful enforcement. | 3B.5; also 3B.2, 3B.1 |
| [Iran: Two years after ‘Woman Life Freedom’ uprising, impunity for crimes reigns supreme](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/) | Amnesty International | 2024-09-11 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/iran-two-years-after-woman-life-freedom-uprising-impunity-for-crimes-reigns-supreme/ | Amnesty documented continuing violent enforcement of veiling rules, including lethal force against a woman during a car confiscation effort, and said authorities still had not carried out impartial investigations. This supports a pattern of coercive control and impunity. | 3B.5; also 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.1 |
| [Iran: New compulsory veiling law intensifies oppression of women and girls](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/12/iran-new-compulsory-veiling-law-intensifies-oppression-of-women-and-girls/) | Amnesty International | 2024-12-10 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/12/iran-new-compulsory-veiling-law-intensifies-oppression-of-women-and-girls/ | The new veiling law imposed death-penalty exposure, flogging, prison terms, travel bans, and broader enforcement powers for police, intelligence, IRGC, and Basij units. That is a textbook example of using administrative/security law as a tool of coercion and collective discipline. | 3B.5; also 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4 |
| [Iran’s leader grants clemency to 2,654 inmates, including foreign nationals](https://english.news.cn/20240617/61af4b6135bc4f07bd0d76069a67ffe7/c.html) | Xinhua | 2024-06-17 | https://english.news.cn/20240617/61af4b6135bc4f07bd0d76069a67ffe7/c.html | Khamenei approved pardons or commutations for 2,654 inmates, including 53 security-charge prisoners and 30 foreign nationals. This is the clearest positive evidence, but it is discretionary clemency, not a structural safeguard or independent accountability mechanism. | 3B.5; also 3B.1 |
| [Leader approves pardoning, commuting sentences of about 3,000 Iranian convicts](https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2024/09/20/733636/Leader-approves-pardoning-convicts) | Press TV | 2024-09-20 | https://www.presstv.ir/Detail/2024/09/20/733636/Leader-approves-pardoning-convicts | Khamenei approved pardons or commutations for 2,887 convicts, including some security-related cases and minors. Positive only at the margin: it shows episodic mitigation of punishment, but not lawful restraint of coercive state power. | 3B.5; also 3B.1 |

**Search gap**
- I found no reliable 2024 evidence that Khamenei built or meaningfully expanded a narrow, lawful emergency-powers framework with civilian oversight, complaint handling, or independent review of abuse.
- The positive evidence is limited to discretionary pardons/commutations and does not show restraint of police, intelligence, or administrative coercion.
- The strongest available evidence points the other way: expanded surveillance, compulsory veiling enforcement, punitive penalties, and broad security-agency involvement.
